h1: Bualuang Hotel Ang Thong — detached garden bungalow rooms, quiet, easy parking, pet-friendly
intro: If you want a place in Ang Thong where you can park right outside your door — no lift needed — with rooms set as detached buildings scattered through a garden so it feels like a small resort, Bualuang Hotel (Bualuang Hotel Ang Thong) is a name passing travellers mention often. It's a 27-room hotel on Ayutthaya-Ang Thong Road in Posa, a few steps from a 7-Eleven and close to Ang Thong Hospital and the Chao Phraya River. Some buildings have been renovated, others show their age, but rates from about ฿500/night and a pet-friendly policy keep it on the shortlist.

body.html: What sets Bualuang Hotel apart from a typical in-town block is its resort-style layout. The rooms aren't stacked in a tower but spread as detached buildings through a garden, so you can park right outside your door without dragging bags into a lift. Self-drivers and families like this a lot — it's more convenient and feels more private than other hotels at the same price. Leafy trees surround the grounds, and it's quiet at night.

The location works well. The hotel sits on Ayutthaya-Ang Thong Road in Posa, a few steps from a 7-Eleven, with made-to-order food stalls at local prices nearby. It's only a few minutes' drive into central Ang Thong, the market and the Chao Phraya River, and Ang Thong Hospital is close by in case of need. It suits travellers using Ang Thong as a stopover heading north or to Ayutthaya more than those who want to wander the town centre on foot, since walkable shops are limited.

Rooms range from Standard large-bed and twin types up to a 35-40 sqm Premier Family Room with two queen beds, good for families. What real reviews consistently praise is that the renovated-zone rooms are clean, the beds are soft, and the detached layout makes it nice and quiet. Each room has air-con, a TV, hot water and basic amenities. Staff come across as friendly and helpful, as many guests note.

"You can park right outside the room, the renovated-zone rooms are clean, and it's quiet because they're separate buildings. Close to a 7-Eleven, friendly staff — good value for five or six hundred baht."

To be honest, the hotel has two clearly different room zones. The older zone shows its age — faded curtains, dated furniture — and some reviews report weak water flow, broken showerheads, or bathrooms that weren't fully cleaned. In-room power outlets are sparse too, with some rooms having just one. If you want a room in good condition, it's worth calling or messaging ahead to request a 'renovated-zone room' to lower the chance of getting an older one.

One more thing to know: facilities are kept simple — no pool or gym. There's a basic breakfast, free parking, 24-hour room service and a small coffee shop. The rare upside is that it's pet-friendly, which is ideal if you're travelling with a dog or cat.

Overall Bualuang Hotel scores 7.7 out of 10 on Trip.com from around 33 real reviews, rating especially well for location and service. It isn't a luxury hotel, but measured on quiet detached garden rooms, easy parking, a pet-friendly policy and a starting rate near ฿500 (climbing to about ฿870-1,200 by season and room type), it does the job of an overnight or business-trip base in Ang Thong nicely on a comfortable budget — as long as you pick the right, newer room zone.

honestSummary: Bualuang Hotel is a sensible pick for travellers who want a quiet detached room, easy parking and the option to bring a pet, all on a budget — an in-town spot near a 7-Eleven and the hospital with friendly service. The trade-off is inconsistent room condition; the older zone shows its age, so request a renovated-zone room before booking.
honestChecks: If you want a room in reliably good condition — the hotel has two zones, old and new, that differ noticeably → call or message to request a 'renovated-zone room' in advance rather than leaving it to chance.

If you want to explore the town centre on foot — this is on a main road with limited walkable shops and is car-oriented → for in-town strolling, look at Suphorn Grand or IKKYU2 in the city centre instead.
If you need to charge several devices — in-room outlets are sparse, some rooms with just one → bring a short power strip for peace of mind.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Bualuang Hotel Ang Thong

faq.q: Where is Bualuang Hotel in Ang Thong, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Bualuang Hotel is at 15/1 Ayutthaya-Ang Thong Road, Posa, Mueang Ang Thong. It's a few steps from a 7-Eleven and close to Ang Thong Hospital and the Chao Phraya River, with central Ang Thong and the market just a few minutes' drive away.

faq.q: How much does Bualuang Hotel cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start from about ฿500/night for a Standard room. Options run from Standard large-bed and twin rooms up to a 35-40 sqm Premier Family Room for families. Prices climb to around ฿870-1,200 by season and room type, so compare a few platforms before booking.
Yes — the hotel welcomes pets, which is rare at this price. It's best to notify them ahead and ask about any conditions or fees so they can assign a suitable room for travelling with your pet.

faq.q: What are the rooms like — are they old?
faq.a: Rooms are detached buildings in a garden, so you can park at your door and it's quiet. That said, there are two zones, old and new, that differ noticeably — the newer zone is clean with soft beds, while the older one shows its age and some rooms have weak water flow. Request a renovated-zone room when booking.
Yes — free parking, and you can park right outside your room because the rooms are detached buildings. It's ideal for self-drivers with plenty of luggage, with no lift to deal with.

faq.q: Who is Bualuang Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's a good fit for drivers passing through, pet owners, or families who want a quiet detached room on a budget. It isn't about luxury or full facilities, but parking is easy, it's private, and the in-town location works — just pick a newer room zone.
